chunks: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from one of his learned companions (the jurists) who said:
When Allah created Paradise, and made its rivers flow, and dangled its fruits and ornaments, He said: 'By My might, a miser will never be allowed into you.'
ai.seo_question: Why is a miser forbidden from entering Paradise according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, the Creator’s declaration that a miser shall not dwell in Paradise underscores the Shia emphasis on *karam* (generosity) as a defining spiritual attribute of the faithful. This narration links the physical beauty of Jannah with the moral purity of its inhabitants, reflecting the broader theological view that inner character determines eternal destiny.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 10.Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from one of his learned companions who said, “
When Allah created Paradise, and made its rivers flow, and dangled its fruits and ornaments, He said [to it], ‘[I swear] by My might, a miser will never be allowed into My company within you.’”
